1.1
GENERAL
DESCRIPTION
OF
COMPRESSOR
Air
Compressor
machine
that
decreases
the
volume
and
increases
the
pressure
of
a
quantity
of
air
by
mechanical
means.
Air
thus
compressed
possesses
great
potential
energy,
because
when
the
external
pressure
is
removed,
the
air
expands
rapidly.
The
controlled
expansive
force
of
compressed
air
is
used
in
many
ways
and
provides
the
motive
force
for
air
motors
and
tools,
including
pneumatic
hammers,
air
drills,
sandblasting
machines,
and
paint
sprayers.
Air
compressors
are
of
two
general
types:
reciprocating
and
rotating.
In
a
reciprocating,
or
displacement,
compressor
(see
Fig.
1),
which
is
used
to
produce
high
pressures,
the
air
is
compressed
by
the
action
of
a
piston
in
a
cylinder.
When
the
piston
moves
to
the
right,
air
flows
into
the
cylinder
through
the
intake
valve;
when
the
piston
moves
to
the
left,
the
air
is
compressed
and
forced
through
an
output-control
valve
into
a
reservoir
or
storage
tank.

As
air
is
compressed
it
is
also
heated.
Air
molecules
tend
to
collide
more
often
with
each
other
in
a
smaller
space,
and
the
energy
produced
by
these
collisions
is
evident
as
heat.
This
heat
is
undesirable
in
the
compression
process,
so
the
air
may
be
cooled
on
the
way
to
the
reservoir
by
circulating
air
or
water.
For
high-pressure
compressed
air,
several
stages
of
compression
may
be
employed,
with
the
air
being
further
compressed
in
each
cylinder
and
cooled
before
each
stage.

2.1
GENERAL
DESCRIPTION
The
PPI
Diaphragm
Compressor
is
a
combination
of
two
systems
—
a
hydraulic
system
and
a
gas
compression
system.
A
metal
diaphragm
group
is
the
isolating
component
between
these
two
systems.
The
gas
compression
system
consists
of
three
flat
metal
diaphragms
which
are
clamped
between
two
precisely
contoured,
concave
cavities
and
the
process
gas
inlet
and
outlet
check
valves.
The
hydraulic
system
includes
a
motor
—
driven
crankshaft
which
reciprocated
a
piston
in
the
hydraulic
fluid
medium.
This
positive
displacement
piston
causes
the
hydraulic
fluid
to
be
pulsed
against
the
lower
side
of
the
diaphragm
group,
which
in
turn
causes
the
diaphragm
group
to
sweep
the
cavity,
displacing
the
process
gas.
The
other
components
of
the
hydraulic
system
are
the
hydraulic
check
valve,
the
hydraulic
system
from
the
feed
lines
as
the
fluid
is
being
compressed.
The
hydraulic
over
pump
valve
is
basically
a
pressure
relief
device
that
assures
that
the
hydraulic
pressure
is
such
that
the
diaphragms
mist
fully
displace
the
cavity
on
each
stroke.
The
automatic
injection
pump
ensures
that
the
hydraulic
system
is
always
full
for
the
compression
stroke
and
provides
for
fast
priming
after
extended
compressor
shutdowns.
2.2
THEORY
OF
OPERATION
A
full
cycle
of
operation
for
the
diaphragm
compressor
begins
with
the
diaphragm
group
fully
deflected
to
the
bottom
of
the
cavity
by
the
process
suction
pressure.
The
hydraulic
piston
is
at
bottom
dead
center
(
BDC
)
and
the
hydraulic
system
has
just
received
the
output
of
a
single
stoke
of
the
automatic
hydraulic
fluid
injection
pump.
On
the
process
side
of
the
diaphragm
group,
the
cavity
is
now
filled
at
a
given
suction
pressure
level
with
the
process
gas,
which
has
entered
through
the
inlet
check
valve.
As
the
crankshaft
rotates
and
the
hydraulic
piston
moves
from
its
bottom
dead
center
position
towards
top
dead
center,
(TDC
)
the
hydraulic
pressure
increases.
This
occurs
since
the
hydraulic
system
injection
and
relief
lines
are
blocked
by
the
hydraulic
check
valve
and
hydraulic
over
pump
valve,
respectively.
As
the
piston
continues
towards
top
dead
center,
and
as
the
hydraulic
pressure
reaches
the
pressure
level
of
the
process
gas
in
the
cavity
reaches
the
pressure
level
downstream
of
the
discharge
check
valve,
that
check
valve
opens
and
the
process
gas
is
discharged
from
the
cavity,
With
the
diaphragm
group
in
this
fully
deflected
discharge
position,
the
piston
still
has
a
certain
amount
of
travel
required
to
reach
its
TDC
position.
As
the
piston
moves
to
TDC,
this
additional
hydraulic
fluid
volume
is
“over
pumped”
through
the
hydraulic
relief
valve,
which
is
set
at
a
pressure
level
above
desired
process
gas
discharge
pressure.
At
this
point,
the
compression
portion
of
the
cycle
has
been
completed.

devices.
The
programmable
controller
is
programmed
using
a
software
package
licensed
for
ICI
from

which
operates
on
a
personal
computer
(by
others)
and
downloads
to
the
programmable
controller
via
an
RS-232
interface.
Programming
is
done
in
"ladder-logic"
format.
The
control
system
facilities
Lead
/
Lag
control
of
the
compressors
on
the
skid.
The
various
control
schemes
are
described
below.
4.2
LEAD
/
LAG
The
intent
of
the
compressor
control
system
is
maintain
gas
at
a
specified
pressure.
The
lead
/
Lag
control
algorithm
allows
an
operator
to
select
which
compressor
will
normally
be
used
to
provide
gas
at
the
desired
pressure.
The
compressor
designated
as
"Lead"
will
always
be
used
whenever
the
system
requires
pressurization.
The
"Lag"
compressor
will
only
active
in
the
event
the
lead
compressor
can
not
keep
up
with
the
demand
of
the
system.
To
facilitate
this,
the
control
panel
is
provided
with
a
selector
switch
to
determine
which
compressor
will
function
as
the
lead
unit.
The
selector
switch
can
be
changed
at
any
time.
However,
in
the
event
the
'Lead'
switch
is
changed
for
a
compressor,
which
is
manning’
the
lead
status
will
not
change
until
the
demand
is
satisfied
and
the
compressor
shuts
off.
If
the
Lead
compressor
chosen
is
not
tamed
on
(Compressor
ON
/
Off
switch
in
Off
position).
The
only
compressor
enabled
will
function
as
the
lead
unit.

4.3
AUTO
/MANUAL
:
An
Auto
/
Manual
switch
is
provided
on
each
panel.
The
automatic
position

lead/lag
control

compressor
as

above.
The
manual
position

Safety

of
operation
4.4
SAFETY
INTERLOCKS:
A
number
of
devices
are
included
on
the
compressor
skid
to
provide
automatic
shutdown
in
the
event
of
a
safety
problem.
Automatic
shutdown
of
the
compressors
occurs
in
the
event
of
a
diaphragm
leak
detection,
high-high
discharge
pressure
and
high-high
discharge
temperature.
Once
this
occurs,
the
alarm
relay
output
will
be
energized.
The
relay
will
stay
energized
until
the
compressors
are
turned
off
(Compressor
ON/OFF
switch
to
off).
Also,
a
start
up
interlock
is
provided
for
the
low
oil
temperature
switch,
in
that,
the
compressor
will
be
prevented
from
starting
until
the
temperature
switch
is
closed
to
signify
the
oil
temperature
is
above
the
switch's
set
point.
4.5
ALARMS
Each
compressor
is
provide
with
field
devices
to
annunciate
an
alarm
condition
on
the
compressor.
The
PLC
monitors
the
status
of
the
field
devices
continuously.
If
an
alarm
switch
becomes
active
or
the
transmitters
exceed
the
pro-programmed
(at
the
factory)
alarm
points
the
PLC
will
alert
an
alarm
condition
by
turning
on
the
appropriate
light
on
the
front
panel
and
energizing
the
alarm
relay.
In
the
case
of
the
process
transmitters
(Discharge
pressure
and
Temperature)
the
alarm
set
points
are
preprogrammed
into
the
PLC
at
the
valves
specified
by
the
user.
The
alarm
relay
output
will
also
be
energized
for
a
automatic
shutdown.
The
alarm
relay
will
reset
when
all
the
alarm
conditions
disappear
or
the
compressor
or
PLC
is
shutdown.

INLET
SOLENOID
VALVE
The
skid
is

with
inlet
solenoid
valves
on

The

4.8
PRESSURE
TRANSMITTERS
The
system
incorporates
a
watchdog
for
the
pressure
transmitter
signals.
If
a
1%
deviation
exists
between
the
signals
the
system
will
shutdown
and
alarm
at
the
annunciator.
4.9
LOCAL
CONTROL
PANELS
A
local
control
panel
is
located
on
the
compressor
skid.
The
local
station
allows
an
operator
to
start
and
stop
each
compressor
and
to
determine
the
mode
(Hand-Off-Auto)
of
operation.
The
local
station
will
override
the
main
(remote)
control
panel
switches.
That
is,
the
remote
panel
will
not
be
able
to
the
compressor
unless
the
local
station
is
in
the
"Auto"
position.
All
local
switches
will
be
interfaced
to
the
PLC
controller,
so
that
,
all
safety
interlocks
will
be
valid
regardless
of
the
mode
of
operation
of
the
compressor.
